# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — enrich WRITE-tool returns with exact $ + auto-correct booking payment split
- Changes I made:
  - tools.py `update_reservation_flights`: return `{**reservation.model_dump(), "payment_summary": ...}` stating exact refund/charge (= net × passengers). Cluster: task 11 (DB already correct, COMMUNICATE=0 because agent quoted per-passenger $1748 not total $5244).
  - tools.py `update_reservation_baggages`, `cancel_reservation`, `book_reservation`: same `payment_summary` enrichment (exact $ charged/refunded).
  - tools.py `book_reservation`: in-body auto-correct guard — when provided payment amounts ≠ computed total AND exactly one credit card is present, set the credit card amount to absorb the remainder (≥0). Cluster: task 25 (agent's split summed to 299 vs true 375; tool errored; agent re-asked; user "Yes.###STOP###" before retry). Also refreshes reservation.payment_history to the corrected amounts.
  - tools.py `book_reservation`: sharpened payment_methods / flights / passengers param docs for the mid reader.
  - policy.md: 7 additive rules — read-first (get_reservation_details/get_user_details before proposing); total = per-passenger × passenger count (worked ex → 5244); copy the return's payment_summary number; act on the first "yes" (no second confirmation); retry immediately on "does not add up"; payment split (credit card absorbs remainder); full passenger list with worked example (task 40).
- Expected effect + safety:
  - Task 11 → COMMUNICATE passes (return states "5244", COMMUNICATE is a substring match on assistant messages). DB already 1.0. Verified.
  - Task 25 → first booking call now writes gold split [gift 128, credit 247], total 375. Verified against live DB.
  - SAFE: enriched returns don't touch DB (DB check hashes db.model_dump(), not the return) and passing tasks 12/19/37 have no COMMUNICATE check. Auto-correct guard fires ONLY on a sum mismatch, which a currently-passing booking never has (verified SAFETY1); with no credit card it still raises the original error (SAFETY2). Policy edits are additive knowledge/procedure and loosen no permission/refusal rule.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none (seed iteration).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: (a) narrated-then-###STOP### with no write executed (40, 23) — environment terminates right after the user's "yes"; cannot force a tool call from code; only lever tried is a policy "act immediately on yes" rule. (b) task/route misunderstanding at conversation start (8, 17) — agent identifies the wrong reservation / tries to book a new trip.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration: if 11 & 25 accepted, attack the narrated-without-action cluster — consider whether a composite "confirm+execute" pattern is expressible, or measure whether the policy "act on yes" rule alone moved 40/23. For 8/17, investigate whether an early get_user_details + enumerate-all-reservations loop tool helps the agent find the right reservation.
